**1. Observation‑schedule design** | Shift | Approx. number of nurses (assumption) | % of unit workforce | Monthly observations (40 × %) | Observations per month | |-------|--------------------------------------|---------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------| | Morning (7 – 15 h) | 12 | 37 % | 0.37 × 40 ≈ **15** | 15 | | Evening (15 – 23 h) | 10 | 31 % | 0.31 × 40 ≈ **12** | 12 | | Night (23 – 7 h) | 10 | 31 % | 0.31 × 40 ≈ **13** | 13 | *If the actual shift‑distribution differs, replace the “Approx. number of nurses” column with the real counts and recompute the percentages accordingly.* The two auditors will split each shift’s quota roughly in half (e.g., Auditor A: 8 morning, 6 evening, 7 night; Auditor B: 7 morning, 6 evening, 6 night). **2. What each auditor must record for a valid observation** | Item | Description | Why it matters | |------|-------------|----------------| | **Date & time stamp** | Exact date and clock‑time of the moment. | Enables temporal trend analysis. | | **Shift identifier** (Morning/Evening/Night) | Indicates which shift the observation belongs to. | Allows shift‑wise compliance comparison. | | **Nurse identifier** (e.g., badge number or anonymised code) | Who performed the hand‑hygiene act. | Enables individual feedback and trend tracking. | | **Patient location/room** | Bed number or unit area. | Contextualises exposure risk. | | **WHO “Five Moments” category** (1–5) | Which moment was observed:
1 = before patient contact, 2 = before aseptic task, 3 = after body fluid exposure, 4 = after patient contact, 5 = after contact with surroundings. | Ensures the audit covers all critical moments. | | **Hand‑hygiene action performed?** (Yes/No) | Whether hand hygiene was carried out at that moment. | Core compliance metric. | | **Product used** (soap, alcohol‑based rub, etc.) | Type of product applied. | Helps assess adherence to policy and product availability. | | **Reason for non‑compliance** (if applicable) | Short note: “time pressure”, “product unavailable”, “forgot”, etc. | Drives targeted interventions. | | **Auditor initials & signature** | Who recorded the observation. | Accountability and data integrity. | *All fields must be filled in real time; a missing field invalidates the observation.* **3. Presenting monthly results to the unit** 1. **Summary dashboard (one‑page PDF or PowerPoint slide)** * Overall compliance:  % of all moments where hand hygiene was performed. * Compliance by moment: bar chart showing % for Moments 1–5. * Shift comparison: side‑by‑side bars for Morning, Evening, Night. * Trend line (if data from previous months available). 2. **Detailed report** (PDF) – 3–4 pages * **Executive summary** – key findings and action items. * **Methodology** – audit scope, number of observations, auditor training. * **Results table** – raw counts per moment, per shift, overall compliance. * **Root‑cause analysis** – most common reasons for non‑compliance (pie chart). * **Recommendations** – e.g., “increase product availability in night shift”, “time‑management training”. 3. **Unit meeting presentation** * Use the dashboard slide to spark discussion. * Highlight any significant deviations from target compliance (> 90 % is typical WHO benchmark). * Invite nurses to share observations and propose solutions. 4. **Follow‑up plan** – schedule next audit cycle, assign responsibilities for addressing identified gaps, set a target improvement (e.g., +5 % compliance by next month). --- *All figures above are derived from the data supplied in the question; if your shift staffing differs, adjust the percentages accordingly.*
